messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: P0 - serving runtime errors + degraded throughput in us-east-1 (customers affected)

emma_oncall: acked. I'm on it. pinging runtime + net oncall.

raj_sre: seeing a spike of CUDA OOMs on several serve pods and rapid container restarts. Also token latency up ~3-4x. Full stack traces attached to pods.

lina_runtime: logs show inference worker failing allocation followed by `SIGABRT` in the allocator. But interestingly, kvcache/kvserver errors precede the OOMs. Possible cascading root cause.

marta_neteng: ib counters show sustained retransmit counts and RNR (receiver not ready) responses on the mlx5 fabric for rack 3. `ibstat` shows intermittent link state changes on two top-of-rack switches.

emma_oncall: customer impact? any specific tenants?

satish_cs: CS: we have 3 paying customers reporting 5xxs and increased timeouts in the last 12m. Early E2E: image-gen partners hitting partial responses.

raj_sre: quick checks I ran: `kubectl get pods -n serve -o wide | grep CrashLoop` -> 6 pods in crashloop across nodes gce-inf-03/04/07. `dmesg` on nodes shows `mlx5_core` kernel messages and `ib_srq` warnings.

raj_sre: pasted commands I ran:```bash
# pod health
kubectl get pods -n serve -o wide
# check kernel logs
ssh gce-inf-03 sudo journalctl -k -u kubelet --since "15m" | tail -n 200
# ib / mlx status
ssh gce-inf-03 sudo ibstat -l && sudo ethtool -S ens5 | grep -E "rx_errors|tx_errors|retransmit"
```

lina_runtime: replication: when a node loses a couple of IB packets the runtime stalls on KV cache sync; that blocks allocation fastpaths and causes OOMs as requests queue and exceed workspace. We have a mitigation path: force-serving fallback to local non-distributed kvcache and drop cross-node KV sync for a short window.

emma_oncall: agreed. Plan: 1) Limit traffic to affected pool, 2) Enable runtime local-kvcache fallback on the crashed nodes, 3) Route new requests to healthy nodes and hosted fallback, 4) Net team to attempt fabric sanity (MTU / port reset).

marta_neteng: starting network triage. I'll check switch counters and will do a port flap test on suspected ports. If we see a hardware link issue we'll move traffic away. Considering MTU rollback from 4096 to 2048 on that ToR to avoid fragmentation.

raj_sre: I'm going to cordon + drain the most unstable nodes to reduce restart churn. Command: `kubectl cordon gce-inf-03 && kubectl drain gce-inf-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force`

lina_runtime: hold on drain for gce-inf-03 for 30s — I'm going to flip the kvcache flag first on pods still alive: set env var `REDWOOD_ENABLE_DIST_KVCACHE=false` via rollout patch on the deployment for pool-serving-1 so new pods come up without distributed kvcache.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: `patch deployment pool-serving-1 -n serve --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"rollback-token":"2119990001"}},"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"serve","env":[{"name":"REDWOOD_ENABLE_DIST_KVCACHE","value":"false"}]}]}}}}'`

emma_oncall: raj + lina coordinate: raj cordon/drain after deploy-bot confirms new pods are scheduled. marta, keep us updated on fabric actions.

marta_neteng: quick wins attempted: performed soft port reset on ToR-3 ports 12/13. Observed reduction in retransmits by ~60% on one port. Running `ethtool -K` tweaks to disable GSO on that interface temporarily to avoid large seg offloads triggering hw issues.

marta_neteng: command logs:```console
# on switch
show counters interface 3/12
# on host
sudo ethtool -K ens5 gso off gro off tso off
sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=134217728
```

raj_sre: new pods with `REDWOOD_ENABLE_DIST_KVCACHE=false` are coming up on gce-inf-05/06 (healthy nodes). CrashLoop count on affected nodes stopped growing.

lina_runtime: good sign. Initiating runtime route change: shift 40% of new production traffic for pool-serving-1 to hosted-fallback cluster in us-east-1 while we stabilize. This is done via router feature-flag `route_override.pool-serving-1=hosted-fallback:0.4`.

emma_oncall: patching route now.

deploy-bot: router update applied: `route_override.pool-serving-1=hosted-fallback:0.4` by emma_oncall (change id r-211999-01).

satish_cs: notifying impacted customers: sending short status update and ETA ~2h. Will advise that we are routing some traffic to hosted fallback and asking for logs.

marta_neteng: follow-up: on ToR 3 we see sporadic packet reordering under load — likely BIOS/fw interplay. I've opened a ticket with the cloud provider for firmware rollback on target nodes.

lina_runtime: we should also apply a guardrail in runtime to drop requests that hit > 5s stall on KV sync to prevent memory accumulation. Opening a quick patch to return an early 503 for those cases.

raj_sre: I applied the guardrail via configmap patch: `runtime-config.kv_sync_timeout_ms=5000` and restarted the sidecars on the remaining nodes.

emma_oncall: anything else for customer-facing messaging?

satish_cs: we'll send an update once we confirm packet error rate stabilizes below threshold and all crashloops stopped. Current ticket: partial degradation, some 5xx for heavy-model jobs.

marta_neteng: fab status: retransmits trending down but still elevated on two NICs; vendor performing fw rollback. I'll post progress.

deploy-bot: alert: `pool-serving-1` deployment scaled from 60 -> 80 to shift load during draining.

lina_runtime: memory pressure is down 70% after the kvcache toggle and draining unstable nodes. OOM events stopped approx 7m after changes. We see a drop in queue length in runtime metrics.

emma_oncall: ok timeline so far: 00:00 pager, 00:02 ack, 00:06 cordon/drain planned after kvcache flip, 00:12 route override, 00:20 guardrail and scale.

raj_sre: next steps: keep fabric on watch, coordinate vendor fw rollout, gradual uncordon after vendor confirms fix. We'll also run stress test (`wrk` + pktgen) to validate under load.

marta_neteng: vendor confirmed fw rollback scheduled for 00:50. After that we'll re-enable GSO/TFO and test.

emma_oncall: oncall handoff: I'm starting my 20m handover to @raj_sre (night shift). Key points: kvcache disabled for pool-serving-1, router override to hosted-fallback at 40%, nodes gce-inf-03/04/07 are drained, vendor fw rollback in progress, CS notified.

raj_sre: ack handoff. I'll monitor for regressions and be prepared to increase fallback to 80% if error rates climb.

satish_cs: I'll keep customers updated; asked for specific request IDs for support triage.

lina_runtime: opened post-incident issue: `PI-211999` capturing follow-ups: - automated test to simulate IB packet loss, - runtime kvcache better fallback logic, - tighter memory caps per-request.

marta_neteng: vendor reports fw rollback completed at 00:55 and NICs passed self-tests. Re-enabled GSO/TFO and observed no spike in retransmits after validation traffic.

raj_sre: uncordoning gce-inf-03 and rescheduling pods now. Will watch for regressions for 30m before fully reverting kvcache flag.

deploy-bot: rollback token r-211999-01 can be used to revert router override.

emma_oncall: quick post-mortem notes while fresh: primary trigger: NIC firmware/hw interaction causing packet retransmits -> KV sync stalls -> runtime queueing -> OOMs and container crashes. Mitigations: local-kvcache fallback, route to hosted fallback, cordon/drain unstable nodes, NIC fw rollback.

satish_cs: customer update sent at 01:10 with summary + mitigation steps. No escalations to legal.

lina_runtime: closing incident runbook checklist: metrics back to baseline, no CrashLoop pods, error rate within SLO. Moving to monitoring phase.

emma_oncall: incident cleared to monitor. Leaving thread open for 2h for final validation. Good work team :clap:
